description:

description:
Halloween: The Game is the latest asymmetrical horror game from IllFonic. It features the typical genre staples, including the familiar PvP-based loop--where players, acting as civilians, must escape a given location while being pursued by a player-controlled monster. Fans of the genre should know what to expect. What makes Halloween: The Game stand out, however, is in how it incorporates NPCs into the mix, as well as key elements from the popular slasher franchise. 

IllFonic has created a survival horror experience that mirrors its source material. Because of this, Halloween: The Game is more about stepping into a role than playing hide-and-seek with Michael Myers. author: Steve Watts
description: In a sea of Legend of Zelda homages, 2018's Moonlighter stood out with its lovely art style and a cool hook: What if the loot you gather on your dungeon-delving adventures wasn't just power-ups, but the wares you sell as part of your day job? Following Moonlighter's release, a number of smaller games, like Cult of the Lamb and Dave the Diver, have found success in complementing action mechanics with light management elements, so it's clearly a combo that works. It would have been easy for developer Digital Sun to simply give us a shinier, more polished version of that original concept in a sequel. Instead, Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault, which has just released in version 1.0 after an early access period, surprisingly rethinks what a Moonlighter game is at its very core. That makes it comfortably live alongside the original, offering an experience that's distinct enough to enjoy both--or to come to the series anew without feeling lost.
title: Moonlighter 2 Feels Like An Entirely Different Game, For Better And Worse

description:
As the platform that gets the lion's share of PC game sales, Steam naturally makes a lot of money every year from commissions, publishing fees, and more through its storefront. But how much cash has it made so far in 2026? Unsurprisingly, enough dough to buy Valve co-founder Gabe Newell a few more superyachts. According to the head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, Rhys Elliot, Steam has made $15 billion in 2026, and with a massive period of high-profile game releases around the corner, that number is likely to surge even higher before the year is over.

description:
What's the biggest question about Grand Theft Auto 6? Easily Rockstar's plans for GTA Online, and how it'll factor into the post-launch plans of GTA 6. Considering just how consistently popular GTA Online has been for the developer, it is strange that Rockstar has yet to publicly comment on the anticipated multiplayer mode, as it has so far only focused on talking about the "single-player experience" of GTA 6. And that could be a major problem for the franchise.

As Valve veteran Chet Faliszek pointed out, Rockstar might be caught between a rock and a hard place.
